# `basket ai` — delegating to an external AI agent

`basket ai` sends a handoff/task file to an external agent CLI in non-interactive mode and collects the response as a response-handoff. It lets any agent or operator use additional model capacity (Kimi/Moonshot, models via OpenRouter — including Claude — or Claude Code) without copying prompts between terminals. Implementation: `src/basket_cli/ai.py`; docs: `docs/agentic/basket-ai-agent-cli.md`.

## Usage

```bash
basket ai \
  --type kimi \
  --model kimi-k3 \
  --handoff /path/to/handoff.md \
  --session-context "additional context or path to a context file" \
  --response-handoff /path/to/response.md \
  --notify true
```

- `--handoff` (required): task file sent to the agent.
- `--session-context`: inline text **or** path to a file; prepended to the prompt in a `BEGIN/END CONTEXT` block.
- `--response-handoff`: response destination (atomic write, metadata header with backend/model/source/timestamp/exit code). Recommended: a file under the workspace `handoff/outbox/` or `handoff/inbox/`, following the handoff protocol (rule 02).
- `--type kimi|claude` (default `kimi`; alias `--backend`).
- `--model`: model alias. Default for kimi: `kimi-k3`.
- `--notify [true|false]`: terminal bell + sound + macOS notification on completion (Glass on success, Basso on failure). Accepts a bare flag or a value.
- `--session <id>`: resumes a kimi session (`kimi -S`).
- `--workdir <dir>`: agent cwd (defaults to current cwd).
- `--auto` / `--yolo`: kimi autonomy (tool-call approval). Default is prompt-only (read-only).

`basket AI` (uppercase) is an accepted alias.

## Types and models

- **`kimi`** — `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi -p`. Aliases configured in `~/.kimi-code/config.toml`: `kimi-k3` (default), `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-k2.5`, `kimi-k2-thinking` (Moonshot); `ox-alpha`, `glm-5.3-flash` (OpenRouter). To use Claude models on OpenRouter credits, add a `[models."<name>"]` alias with `provider = "openrouter"` in that config and pass it via `--model`.
- **`claude`** — `claude -p` if the binary is installed; otherwise the command fails with install instructions. If no Claude CLI is available on the machine, use an OpenRouter alias through kimi.

## Credentials

Canonical API keys live in `basketiq-wow/cfg/keys/`:

- `cfg/keys/kimi-api-key.txt` — Moonshot/Kimi.
- `cfg/keys/openrouter-api-key.txt` — OpenRouter (Claude and other models).

`basket ai` does **not** read these keys: it delegates to each CLI's own config (`~/.kimi-code/config.toml`). The `cfg/keys/` files are for bootstrapping a CLI on a new machine or for direct API use when no CLI is available.

## Security — mandatory

- **Never** paste an API key into a prompt, handoff, rule, doc or commit. The values in `cfg/keys/` and `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` are secrets.
- The response-handoff records only metadata (backend, model, paths, timestamp, exit code) — never credentials.
- The agent's exit code propagates: a failure writes the partial response with `exit=N` in the header and returns non-zero.
- Without `--auto`/`--yolo`, the agent runs in prompt-only mode and executes no effectful tools — that is the safe default.
